method: sum of gzip -9 over each module in the route's rel="modulepreload" list, per file, never concatenated
tolerance_basis: 4 builds of identical source, route /, 2026-08-25, this repo: 49193 / 49198 / 49198 / 49205. Range 12 B, and the cause is named - SvelteKit stamps a version string into the entry chunk. 64 B is 5.3x that range; four samples underestimate a true range, so the multiple is the margin. Derived, not measured. If a build ever fails inside 64 B, re-derive it from more builds and more routes rather than nudging it.

/.why: SvelteKit runtime, the app shell, and the reader item chunk every day view shares - item cards, the in-place topic filter and the per-day read mark. It grew 430 B when the archive's search started rendering a result through that same item component: Vite cuts a chunk by which routes use a module, so the shared reader chunk absorbed the archive's search code too. Read as a difference, not an absolute - an untouched base build of this tree read 49,119 B and passed this gate on every route, and the changed one reads 49,549 B on the same machine and the same node.

/<date>/.why: The same runtime, shell and reader item chunk as /, on one day's items, and the same +430 B from that shared chunk. Control on this tree: 48,992 B.

/<date>/<topic>/.why: The same runtime, shell and reader item chunk as /, on one topic of one day, and the same +428 B from that shared chunk. Control on this tree: 49,086 B.

/404.why: Runtime and app shell and nothing route-specific. This is the floor every other route sits on. It fell 105 B in the same chunk re-cut that raised /: one module left this route's preload list. Control on this tree: 40,858 B.

/archive/.why: Runtime and shell plus the archive route, which lists stories and now searches them: the month-index fetch and decode, the newest-first regrouping, the paged list and its Show-more control, the encoder guard, and - new here - the int8 vector decode, the day-payload fetch and cache a result renders from, and the digest's own item component that renders it. That is +4,277 B against an untouched base build of this tree at 45,711 B, and what it buys is 1,763,770 gzipped bytes off the document: the page no longer inlines every committed day. A dynamic import of the item component was measured and rejected on 2026-08-27 - it moves this route to 46,988 B but costs / another 310 B, because a separate chunk compresses worse than the shared one it left.

/console/.why: Runtime and shell plus the console route: hand-written SVG charts and the d3-scale and d3-array arithmetic behind them, the stage-timing decade axis with its minor stubs and its gap-instead-of-plunge run splitting, the Charts table that says what the router cost and what it published on each day, and the What the model did table. It fell 112 B in the archive change's chunk re-cut, having gained nothing of its own. Control on this tree: 66,168 B.

/evals/.why: Runtime and shell plus the stub that moves an old bookmark to /console/. Down 98 B in the same chunk re-cut. Control on this tree: 41,808 B.
